leads_to.evidence: BLS reports that 48 percent of workers with an English degree hold an advanced degree, against 38 percent across all fields. Many go on to teaching, law or other graduate study, so first-year pay understates later earnings.

nearby_pair.evidence: Both are public four-year colleges that admit first-year freshmen through ordinary applications: Queens College through the CUNY application, and New Jersey City University, which admits most applicants, through the Common App.

school_matters.evidence: English graduates spread across many occupations instead of one elite pipeline. Education, training and library jobs, which mostly pay on set scales, are the largest group, so going to a highly selective school adds little to first-year pay.

who_is_counted.evidence: The largest programs include none that are online-only and three that are pooled. They pay below the major's median, which fits mostly new graduates, but research did not confirm their admission requirements.

programs.evidence: Georgetown admits a small share of applicants, and its location in Washington gives graduates access to policy, media and professional employers.
Yale is among the most selective universities in the country, and its graduates are recruited by top employers.
Colgate is a highly selective liberal arts college whose graduates are recruited by top employers.
